summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 1.44/1884)

data.turoyo: <...> Darmone latwo, kətwo darmone ṣunʕi, u Ablaḥḥad ḥaloqo samwo darmone ṣunʕi, i bam mo ḥa (% 1) balki məstafadle. <...>
data.translation: <...> There were no medicines; there were handmade medicines. Ablahhad the barber made handmade medicines; perhaps one in a hundred (1%) benefited. <...>

rationale: First Preterit1; beneficial treatment outcome without an overt source phrase, under the round-1 gloss.

data.turoyo: lašan d məstafdi mu ḥalwo d saymile gweto, nuḥriwo u ṣafuro, meqəm məd yonəq mi emo, w maydiwo u ḥalw... u yalwo d gawe, kəmmile fəršək.
data.translation: Um die Milch zur Käseherstellung zu benutzen, schlachteten sie das Junge, bevor es von der Mutter saugte und nahmen die Mil..., die Biestmilch in seinem Magen, man nennt sie Lab.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; m-marked material resource and purpose.

data.turoyo: W aq qaše kəmmi qəṣayəṣ, b ḥaq daq qadiše, b ḥaq d Mšiḥo, lašan d məstafdo i ǧamaʕa, d kətne yatiwe, ḥatta d oṯe l bolayye kaʔinnahu, kətte yawmo lənne ste hawxa gmənqoli maḥ ḥayani
data.translation: Die Priester erzählen Geschichten, über die Heiligen, über den Messias, damit die Anwesenden, die dort sitzen, davon profitieren, so dass ihnen klar wird, dass es auch für sie einen Tag gibt, an dem sie aus diesem Leben abberufen werden.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; overt collective beneficiary subject and omitted benefit source clarify the meaning.

data.turoyo: <...> Annaqqa u ʕamo məǧbarwo, əzzewo manṭewo, mzabanwo laǧan d məstafəd mene. <...>
data.translation: <...> Then the people were compelled: they would go, bring things, and sell them in order to benefit from them. <...>

rationale: Fourth cumulative Infectum1 example; trade profit and explicit m-source.

data.turoyo: Aṯili rənye ste ḥaṯe d kibi məstafadno bu zabno d gdoṯe bu ʕwodo. Hawxa.
data.translation: New ideas also came to me, which I can use in work in the time to come. Like that.

rationale: Fifth cumulative Infectum1 example; ideas as useful resource and b-work as sphere.

after: (mit m-, auch ohne ausgedrückte Ergänzung) Nutzen ziehen, profitieren; ausnutzen, benutzen;
rationale: The congregation derives benefit without an overt resource phrase (JTM 1.2/15). The old ausnutzen alone suggests only active exploitation; m-marked milk/electricity uses link both readings.

summary: All three occurrences are Infectum in a purposive or desired clause. Preserve the source's stem I for the Arabic X-shaped loan; inherent mə- is not Detransitive marking.
Milk and electricity are m-marked resources. The congregation is the benefiting subject and its source is contextually supplied by the priests' stories.
The Arabic-derived simple verb is contact evidence; no light-verb-plus-noun construction appears here. The 11/148 quotation is already present and is not duplicated.
All seven occurrences checked. Preserve glossary stemI for the Arabic X-shaped loan; inherent mə- is not Detransitive marking. Round-1 gloss widening is retained and not repeated in entry.json.

məstafadle supplies a first l-agent Preterit; the beneficiary is the subject, with treatment as contextual source. Do not equate benefiting with full medical recovery or validate the speaker’s mortality estimate.

The Infectum cell had three examples after round 1; trade and ideas fill it to five. Community benefit from a learned person repeats the prior congregation example; Latin-derived medicine names illustrate a further learned-language resource without requiring another sense.
Modern institutional and language-resource topics extend the same benefit relation. No light-verb construction or independently established new borrowing history is present.
All selected English is the supplied machine translation. Its use in work at 4.I/371 reflects the source’s ordinary useful-resource reading; no editor translation is substituted.
Does a speaker distinguish neutral profitieren from a marked ausnutzen reading in this loan? The corpus supports the neutral benefit relation without establishing two lexical senses.
Does 4.I/163 mean borrowing medicine names from Latin or benefiting from another intervening resource? The complement is contextual, so no Latin-specific sense is proposed.
Does məstafadle in the treatment passage indicate any benefit or recovery? The lexical entry retains neutral benefit, without claiming recovery.
Jan reinforces round 1’s neutral benefit gloss through treatment, trade, learning and usable ideas. Source m- can be explicit or omitted; b u ʕwodo locates the sphere of use.
